title: Meals You Can’t Miss

chapters.description: Cool rice noodles, green fish curry and a fistful of herbs
Freshwater fish steamed with coconut custard and kroeung
Peppery seared beef, crisp vegetables and a sharp lime dip

editorial: Cambodian cuisine is quite distinct from its Southeast Asian neighbours. It relies heavily on fermentation, which makes for strong (almost pungent) flavours that may not be to everyone’s liking. The popular Prahok Ktis and Fish Amok are both fermented fish recipes.

If fermented foods aren’t your thing, then there’s always grilled meats (assuming you want to still indulge in local meals). But the grilled meats aren’t as heavily marinated as say satays in Thailand and Malaysia, and may feel underwhelming if you’re expecting an explosion of flavours.
